Native archives run without Node.js. Download the archive matching your operating system and CPU, verify it with `SHA256SUMS`, extract `dbx-mcp` (or `dbx-mcp.exe`), and configure your MCP client to run it directly.

Two days after rc8, this release is mostly what people running rc8 found: Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint now works from embedding to tool calls, a deployment with a restricted database role gets its vector indexes, and a failing embedding model no longer silences chat memory. The first cut of regression cases for the ontology arrives, and the old ontology growth loop is retired.

Two weeks in which extraction stopped writing into a schema and started writing what documents say, and alignment learned to turn that back into typed facts. The ledger, the interface and the reading of files all moved with it.

## A document is read in its own words

Extraction writes an **open graph** — the subject, the relation phrase as written, the object, the quote it came from — and nothing is bent to fit a class on the way in ([0044](docs/decisions/0044-the-ontology-is-a-view-over-what-documents

- MySQL-compatible warehouses can be mounted — one driver reaches TiDB, OceanBase, Doris and StarRocks ([#315](https://github.com/deeplethe/utopia/pull/315), [#323](https://github.com/deeplethe/utopia/pull/323))
The schema still evolves between versions and migrations only roll forward. Pin `UTOPIA_IMAGE`, and back up the database along with the `data` directory before upgrading.
- A namesake tie now goes to review instead of being decided by the order rows came back from the database ([#329](https://gith

- Deleting a document is an event on the recording axis, not a hole in the database. The document gets a tombstone, its chunks are marked superseded, and nothing is cleared. Only facts whose every source is deleted are retired; a fact another live document vouches for stays. The toast offers Undo, a sync that meets the tombstone while the source still has the file revives it, and re-uploading the same content revives it too. The evidence panel says "source deleted" on a quote whose document is gone. (#273,
Trino (Iceberg / Delta / Hive), Databricks and Snowflake are query engines behind the same trait; the connection string's scheme picks the engine.

Redaction remains a best-effort safety net, not a shell sandbox or a guarantee that every secret is removed. Previously saved history is not rewritten, live tool-call arguments remain executable and unchanged, and incomplete or ambiguous output may delay streaming. See the [coverage and limitations](https://github.com/spences10/my-pi/blob/my-pi%400.9.0/packages/pi-redact/README.md#limitations) and [benchmark report](https://github.com/spences10/my-pi/blob/my-pi%400.9.0/docs/pi-redact-benchmark.md).

### Repeatable tasks and session trace reviews

`@spences10/pi-harness 0.3.1` adds two native Pi skills:

- `review-session-trace` reviews execution evidence, including failures, retries and user corrections, rather than trusting the final summary. Reviews follow task boundaries and session branches, with abandoned attempts considered separately.

All six harness tools now use Pi's built-in codemode exposure instead of being declared individually to the model by default. Call them through scripts, such as `tools.harness_create(...)` and `tools.harness_update(...)`.

Fixes after the first installs.

- AI provider: clear "model not found" and timeout states; Gemini uses the least thinking, so photos are recognized faster
- The sign-in screen names the exact setup error instead of a generic one
- Phone: the meal edit footer stays at the bottom edge; no blurred patch under the iOS status bar
- Desktop: nested settings screens in one column, no duplicate invite action
- Docker: runs as `PUID:PGID` and keeps data in a `./data` folder next to `docker-compose.yml`, with a Syno
- One Docker image for amd64 and arm64, SQLite in one volume
